newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian party says got Dassault gift, firm denies.
newsitem.headline: Belgian party says got Dassault gift, firm denies.

text.p: Belgium's governing Flemish Christian Democratic Party (CVP) on Tuesday confirmed a press report that it was given 1.2 million francs ($40,000) by French aerospace firm Dassault Aviation in 1987.
In Paris, a spokesman for the company denied that Dassault had ever made such a donation. "I can only once again deny it. We are not making any other comment," he said.
In Belgium, CVP spokesman Willy Buijs told Belga news agency: "Until 1989, under the law on party financing, gifts were perfectly legal."

The Belgian daily newspaper De Morgen had said that the independent Oversight Committee had given the Cour de Cassation, Belgium's highest court, a report saying the money was passed over in December 1987 when Wilfried Martens headed the then Christian Democrat-Liberal coalition.
It is not the first time Dassault's name has been connected with money alleged to have been paid to Belgian political parties, but it was the first time it was linked to the CVP.

NATO Secretary General Willy Claes, a government economics minister for the Socialist Party in the late 1980s, was forced to resign in October last year over bribes alleged to have been paid to his party by Dassault and Italian helicopter maker Agusta SpA in exchange for for contracts.
Another Socialist minister at the time, Guy Coeme, was also forced to quit 18 months earlier for the same reasons.
A series of Christian Democrat-Socialist governments have held power in Belgium since early 1988.

In May this year Belgium issued an international arrest warrant for company head Serge Dassault on suspicion of corruption. He has denied allegations he paid 10 million French francs ($2 million) in bribes for a deal to modernise Belgian air force F16 and Mirage fighter jets.
